histology: gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST), SDH-deficient subtype (KIT/PDGFRA wild-type)
stage: ypT3(m)N0M1 — multifocal gastric GIST with a single M1 deposit in the ligament of Treitz; R0 distal gastrectomy + Roux-en-Y; 0/7 nodes; largest mass 7.5 cm; M1 deposit completely resected

biomarkers.name: SDHA L306P
biomarkers.decision_resolution: Germline-vs-somatic determination via paired germline NGS (blood or buccal). Required for genetic counseling and for confidence that the tumor is biallelically SDHA-inactivated (the dominant driver call for KIT/PDGFRA-WT, SDH-deficient GIST).

biomarkers.name: SDHA Y408N
biomarkers.decision_resolution: Tumor NGS variant call at decision-relevant resolution. Combined with the SDHA L306P call, this gives biallelic SDHA inactivation — the canonical SDH-deficient-GIST molecular phenotype.

biomarkers.name: SDHA E350fs
biomarkers.decision_resolution: ctDNA call only — confirm in tumor tissue NGS to establish whether this is a third SDHA hit, a subclonal event, or a ctDNA artifact. Decision relevance: stability of the SDH-deficient driver call.

biomarkers.name: PIK3CA R93W
biomarkers.decision_resolution: Tissue NGS confirmation required. R93W is a non-helical-domain hotspot variant of weaker functional consequence than the canonical E542K/E545K/H1047R hotspots; clinical actionability for PI3Kα inhibitors (alpelisib, inavolisib) is uncertain at R93W.

biomarkers.name: MAP2K1 P124S
biomarkers.decision_resolution: Tissue NGS confirmation required. P124 is a known MAP2K1 activating hotspot — confirmed presence would create a mechanistic rationale for MEK-inhibitor consideration.

biomarkers.name: POLE R1679C
biomarkers.decision_resolution: Germline NGS variant call. R1679 is outside the canonical POLE exonuclease/proofreading domain (P286R / V411L / S459F hotspots); given TMB < 1 mut/Mb and MSS, this is most plausibly a VUS without therapy implications. Cancer-predisposition counseling is still warranted.

biomarkers.name: CD117 (KIT) protein
biomarkers.decision_resolution: IHC. Supports GIST diagnosis; does NOT imply KIT-mutant GIST given the KIT-WT genotype.

biomarkers.name: Desmin
biomarkers.decision_resolution: IHC. Helps exclude smooth-muscle / leiomyosarcoma mimics.

biomarkers.name: SDHB protein
biomarkers.decision_resolution: IHC. INTERPRETIVE CAVEAT: biallelic SDHA inactivation classically destabilizes the SDH complex and produces SDHB-loss-of-staining. Retained SDHB IHC in the face of two SDHA somatic variants (≈85% combined VAF) is unusual; re-cut and re-stain (with a positive internal control) before accepting SDH-proficient phenotype on IHC alone.

biomarkers.name: KIT
biomarkers.decision_resolution: Tumor NGS. Excludes KIT-mutant GIST and the imatinib first-line label tied to exon 11.

biomarkers.name: PDGFRA
biomarkers.decision_resolution: Tumor NGS. Excludes PDGFRA D842V-mutant GIST and the avapritinib label.

biomarkers.name: TMB
biomarkers.decision_resolution: TMB ≥10 mut/Mb required for tumor-agnostic pembrolizumab; <1 mut/Mb does not meet that threshold.

biomarkers.name: MSI status
biomarkers.decision_resolution: MSI-high required for tumor-agnostic ICI (pembrolizumab); MSS effectively excludes that pathway.

biomarkers.name: BRAF
biomarkers.decision_resolution: NGS. Excludes the BRAF V600E-driven WT-GIST subset and BRAF/MEK-inhibitor label.

prior_therapies.regimen: distal gastrectomy with Roux-en-Y reconstruction; R0 resection of multifocal primary gastric GIST + complete resection of M1 deposit at the ligament of Treitz; 0/7 nodes involved

targetable_features.rationale: User-stated targetable phenotype. Mechanistically: SDH loss → succinate accumulation → pseudo-hypoxia / HIF stabilization / global DNA hypermethylation. Decision-relevant for: belzutifan (HIF-2α inhibitor) and DNA-hypomethylating agents (guadecitabine, decitabine) as rational targeted approaches; temozolomide on the basis of single-arm phase-II activity specifically in SDH-deficient GIST; sunitinib/regorafenib/ripretinib as the imatinib-resistant systemic backbone.

User-stated targetable feature. Mechanism: PI3Kα activation; therapeutics include alpelisib and inavolisib. Caveat: R93W is a low-frequency, non-canonical variant with weaker activating consequence than the E542K/E545K/H1047R hotspots — clinical actionability is uncertain and trial enrollment is gated by tissue confirmation.

User-stated targetable feature. Mechanism: MEK1 activating hotspot at P124; therapeutic rationale exists for MEK inhibitors (trametinib, selumetinib, binimetinib) and MEK+RAF combos; clinical evidence in GIST is anecdotal at best, but P124 is a recognized activating site in other histologies.

User-stated. Mechanism would be POLE proofreading deficiency → hypermutation → ICI-responsiveness; however R1679 sits outside the canonical exonuclease domain and the patient is TMB-low + MSS, so the standard POLE-hypermutator therapy rationale does not apply. Listed here for completeness; the decision-relevant action is genetic-counseling referral, not ICI.

targetable_features.feature: KIT/PDGFRA wild-type, KIT-WT GIST molecular subtype
targetable_features.rationale: Negative finding with decision consequences: imatinib first-line response rate is sharply lower in SDH-deficient GIST (~PR rate single-digit %); sunitinib and regorafenib have better activity in this subset. Pulls the systemic-therapy plan away from imatinib-first.
